task: Add a third allowed user_type value, "service_account", so it is accepted from the Keycloak JWT claim and persisted on the CodeMie user record alongside the existing "regular" and "external" values.

key_reasoning.reason: The allowed-value set is independently duplicated in two components — codemie's rest_api.security user_type validator and codemie-enterprise's idp.user_type validator — that must be changed in lockstep across a deliberate zero-coupling architectural boundary between the two repositories, rather than a single shared component.

Both validator modules plus their test suites (base validator tests, enterprise Keycloak IDP tests, enterprise Keycloak-admin migration tests) and a persistence-model comment need updating; no new files are required, but the touched files spread across five-plus directories in two separate repositories rather than one localized area.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M to L: touches a core shared validation utility (the VALID_USER_TYPES allowed-value set), which is duplicated rather than shared, across two repositories that must be kept in sync.

Technical Risk bumped from S to M: user_type is derived from the authentication/IDP claim pipeline and feeds an authorization-adjacent classification (User.is_external_user), matching the 'affects authentication or authorization' red flag.
